segmentName: Activated bleaching earth & bentonite (industrial minerals for oil refining)

market.domesticSlice: figures are global; ~40-45% combined share held by the 5 majors above, rest split among small-scale regional/Indian/Chinese producers

adjacentMarkets.name: Fuller's Earth (broader category)
adjacentMarkets.note: Wet-technology segment ~43.2% of the global Fuller's Earth market (2025), ~$1.21B

structureFacts: ~5-8 kg of activated bleaching earth is consumed per metric ton of refined palm oil — a high-volume, structurally recurring input, not a discretionary purchase.

India imported 16 million tonnes of edible oil in 2025, 99.7% of palm-group volumes in crude (unrefined) form — a large, currently-unmet domestic refining opportunity that would pull directly on this product category if refining capacity expands.
Acid-activated bentonite is described as delivering the lowest cost-per-tonne outcome for bulk edible-oil bleaching under GRAS/EU food-additive clearances, sustaining its dominance over alternatives.

adoptionStructure.note: A recurring industrial-consumable market (bleaching earth is consumed/discarded per refining batch, not a durable good), driven by edible-oil refining volumes — not a subscription or replacement-rate market in the agri-seed sense.

peers.name: Ashapura Perfoclay Limited
peers.note: A much larger, listed peer in the exact same product category (bleaching earth and clay catalyst) — among India's largest bentonite exporters. Real, useful benchmark: net profit grew ~65% YoY on a ~10x-larger revenue base, while Nav Bharati's own EBITDA kept declining over a comparable period.

peersNoteOthers: Other named competitors (20 Microns Limited, Refoil Earth Pvt Ltd, Indian Clay & Mineral Co, HRP Industries, Global Bleach Chem, Korvi Activated Earth, Manek Active Clay) surfaced but no financials were found for them in this research pass.

drivers: Cost-per-tonne is the primary competitive axis in this category — unlike the certification-gated dynamics seen in auto-OEM or medical-device segments, this is closer to a scale/cost commodity game.
Consistent grade/quality control and reliable, prompt delivery are named differentiators among smaller regional suppliers (e.g. Refoil Earth's positioning).
Regulatory clearances (GRAS, EU food-additive status) matter at the product-category level, not as a company-specific certification battle.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Cost-per-tonne competitiveness at consistent quality — not a single gating certification the way IATF 16949 or ISO 13485 function in the other two segments researched.
